issues.description: Loop invariant for valueToMetricFullKey is not stated and diverges from detailedMetricFullKey logic
issues.detail: The new builder runs in lockstep with the entry loop but its invariant ('after iteration i, the builder holds domain plus the chosen segment for each of the first i+1 entries') is never written down. Without an explicit invariant the three-branch if/else (wildcard / matchedUsingValue / default) is hard to verify and easy to break. Add a literate comment stating the invariant and the segment-construction rule.

issues.description: Dead allocation: NewRateLimit is called and immediately overwritten, suggesting confused intent
issues.detail: In the post-loop block, rateLimit is reassigned via NewRateLimit(..., this.statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey), ...) and then Stats is overwritten on the next line with NewStats(enhancedKey). One of the two NewStats calls is pure waste and may register a stats entry under the old key. Either drop the NewRateLimit call or skip the redundant first NewStats; state why a fresh struct is needed.

issues.description: Asymptotically OK but constants doubled: builder runs unconditionally even when no descriptor sets value_to_metric
issues.detail: valueToMetricFullKey is built on every GetLimit call, doing string allocation and comparison per entry, even for configs that never use the new flag. The override is then gated by enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey. A cheap guard ('any descriptor on the path has valueToMetric') would avoid charging every existing user for an opt-in feature. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW on the hot path.

issues.description: Wildcard and default-key branches duplicate identical code; the three-way switch collapses to two cases
issues.detail: Both 'matchedViaWildcard' and 'default key' branches do the same thing: if valueToMetric then key_value else key. The matchedUsingValue branch always emits key_value. The whole block reduces to: if (matchedUsingValue || nextDescriptor.valueToMetric) emit key_value else emit key. The current expansion obscures the invariant and invites divergence on future edits. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT or refactor.

issues.description: Termination edge: 'no descriptor found' branch silently emits entry.Key, masking misconfiguration in the metric
issues.detail: When nextDescriptor is nil the builder still appends '.' + entry.Key to keep the builder deterministic. This means a request that fails to match any descriptor produces a stats key that looks legitimate. Document the choice or fall back to the existing FullKey rather than fabricating a path.

issues.description: No test covers the post-leaf case where additional entries follow the rate-limited descriptor
issues.detail: GetLimit continues iterating after rateLimit is captured; the value_to_metric builder keeps appending. The tests only exercise paths where the leaf descriptor is the last entry. Add a test with trailing entries after the limit-bearing descriptor to confirm the metric key is still what the author intends.

review.summary: The feature is small in scope but the implementation is UNDER-AUDITED: the new metric-key builder runs in parallel with the existing detailedMetricFullKey logic without a stated invariant, and the three-branch case-analysis collapses to a simpler rule once you write the invariant down. There is a redundant NewRateLimit/NewStats pair that allocates twice and may register a stray stats entry under the old key. The builder also pays per-request cost for users who never enable the flag, which is ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW on the hot path. Tests are good for the happy paths but miss the post-leaf-entries case and the nil-descriptor fallback. Add the invariant, collapse the duplicated branches, gate the builder on actual use, and the change becomes clean.
